newsitem.title: UK: NWE GASOLINE BARGES DOWN $9; DEALS AS LOW AS $228.
newsitem.headline: NWE GASOLINE BARGES DOWN $9; DEALS AS LOW AS $228.

text.p: NWE mogas values lost a hefty $9 in early trading on Thursday as crude futures fell below $19 a barrel and mogas dealers reversed the massive jump of recent days.

The recently active Wall Street trader bought at least four first half August Eurograde barge lots at $232, $230 and twice at $228. Some dealers argued bids subsequently fell to $226 but others still saw talk as high as $230.
A second half Eurograde deal was rumoured at $214 as regular mogas was valued $5 below premium unleaded.

There were unconfirmed rumours of a $213 August swap deal, with August value placed at $213-$214, just over $4 below Wednesday's close, but September was seen falling back by a more heavy $4.50-$5 to $196-$198.

PDVSA's Cardon refinery force majeure, confirmed on Wednesday, was seen indirectly contributing to a $5 rise in MTBE quotes to $320-$325, although this was mainly seen as a response to gasoline gains between last Friday and this Wednesday.
